Inglewood, California
  June 18, 2019

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, June 18, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
Authority, and Finance Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority
Secretary/Finance Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as
follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members/Finance
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority
officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Finance
Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority on any item on
the Agenda.

The following persons spoke concerning Agenda Item CI-2, Initiative by Mayor
James T. Butts, Jr., recommending the introduction of an Ordinance amending
Chapter 8 (Business, Trades, and Professions) of the Inglewood Municipal Code
to add a new Article 9 (Housing Protection Initiative) for the regulation of rent
increases and just cause evictions for certain covered residential rental units.

Felicia Ford
No name given
No name given

Morris “Big Money” Griffin
Malcolm Bennet
Willie Agee
O’ Ryan Gould
Ray Davis, 2nd District
Pamela McThamon

  1
 June 18, 2019

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Dotson, and seconded
  by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Morales that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated, June 13, 2019, in the amount of $4,306,747.10,
  are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing
  Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said
  demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  denial of the following claims:

  a) Dawn Goodwin for alleged property damage on February 23, 2019.
  b) Evan Hightower for alleged property damage on February 2, 2019.
  c) Lori McCloud for alleged property damage on December 4, 2018.
  d) Tanya Shuemaker for alleged personal injury on October 25, 2018.
  e) Brian Statler, Sr., for alleged personal injury on March 27, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin and carried that the above listed claims be denied.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member Franklin that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on
  June 4, 2019, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 19-71 ADOPTED – AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2018-
  2019 BUDGET FOR CITY HALL SECURITY UPGRADES. Staff report
  dated June 18, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution
  amending the Fiscal Year 2018-2019 budget to allocate funds for critical City
  Hall Security Upgrades and the development of the new City-wide Emergency
  Operations Plan.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that Resolution No. 19-71 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2018-2019 FISCAL
  YEAR BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  171  ACCESSION APPROVED – PUBLIC ART MURAL BY RICHARDO
  DUFFY. Staff report dated June 18, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval to accession Cosmic Fusion, the public art mural by Ricardo Duffy, into
  the City of Inglewood Public Art Collection, making it eligible for maintenance
  and conservation through the Public Art Fund.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that the City Council does hereby approve accession. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  2
 June 18, 2019

 183  PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDSING INVOICE AUTHORIZED – DEL REY
  PARTY RENTALS. Staff report dated June 18, 2019, was presented
  recommending authorization to pay an outstanding invoice submitted by Del Rey
  Party Rentals for supplies provided for the City of Inglewood’s Earth Day Music
  Festival and Environmental Awareness event held April 20, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that the City Council does hereby authorize payment of invoice in the
  amount of $9,070.92. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes:  None.

 183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 19-215 APPROVED –
  PALP, INC., DBA EXCEL PAVING COMPANY. Staff report dated June 18,
  2019, was presented recommending award of contract and approval of an
  agreement with PALP, Inc., dba Excel Paving Company, for the Van Ness
  Avenue Improvement Project per Bid No. CB-19-08.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement
  No. 19-215 in the amount of $922,680 (includes a 10% project contingency in the
  amount of $83,880). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 131.8  RESOLUTION NO. 19-72 ADOPTED – ADOPTING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2019-2020  CITIZEN  PARTICIPATION  PLAN  FOR  THE
  CONSOLIDATED PLAN AND ANNUAL ACTION PLAN; RESOLUTION
  NO. 19-73 ADOPTING THE CITIZEN PARTICIPATION PLAN FOR THE
  ANNUAL ACTION PLAN PROCESS; PUBLIC HEARING SET FOR
  JULY 9, 2019, – DRAFT FY 2019-2020 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN; PUBLIC
  HEARING SET - DRAFT FY 2018-2019 CONSOLIDATED ANNUAL
  PERFORMANCE EVALUATION REPORT. Staff report dated June 18,
  2019, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution to adopt the Fiscal
  Year 2019-202 Citizen Participation Plan, and set public hearings for Fiscal Year
  2019-2020 the Consolidated Plan Process.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 19-72 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA ADOPTING THE FY2019-2020
  CITIZEN PARTICIPATION PLAN FOR THE CONSOLIDATED
  PLAN AND ANNUAL ACTION PLAN

  2) Adopt Resolution No. 19-73 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,  ADOPTING  THE  CITIZEN
  PARTICIPATION PLAN FOR THE ANNUAL ACTION PLAN PROCESS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  Mayor Butts ordered the Public Hearing set for July 9, 2019, at 2:00 p.m., to
  receive public comments on the Draft FY2019-2020 Annual Action Plan.

  3
 June 18, 2019

  Mayor Butts ordered the Public Hearing set for December 10, 2019, at 2:00 p.m.
  to receive public comments on the Draft FY2018-2019 Consolidated Annual
  Performance Evaluation Report (CAPER).

 219  ORAL REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. City Treasurer, Wanda Brown,
  stated that USA Today (June 13, 2019) had a great article regarding Reverse
  Mortgages, and how they end in foreclosure economic news.

  City Clerk, Yvonne Horton left the Council Chambers at the hour of 2:31 p.m.

 127.2  COUNCIL INITIATIVES:

  Mayor Butts:

  Initiative by Mayor James T. Butts, Jr., recommending the introduction and
  adoption of the second extension of Urgency Interim Ordinance No. 19-07,
  limiting rent increases to 5% per year on certain residential properties within the
  City of Inglewood, for an additional 180 days.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Abstain: Council Member Franklin.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that Ordinance No. 19-12 entitled:

  SECOND  EXTENSION  OF  URGENCY  INTRERIM
  ORDINANCE NO. 19-07 OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, FOR AN ADDITIONAL 180 DAYS
  COMMENCING FROM JUNE 18, 2019, LIMITING CERTAIN
  RESIDENTIAL RENT INCREASES TO NO MORE THAN 5%
  AND REQUIRING JUST CAUSE FOR EVICTIONS

  was introduced by Mayor Butts.

  Furthermore, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby adopt Emergency Ordinance No. 19-12
  entitled:

  SECOND  EXTENSION  OF  URGENCY  INTRERIM
  ORDINANCE NO. 19-07 OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, FOR AN ADDITIONAL 180 DAYS
  COMMENCING FROM JUNE 18, 2019, LIMITING CERTAIN
  RESIDENTIAL RENT INCREASES TO NO MORE THAN 5%
  AND REQUIRING JUST CAUSE FOR EVICTIONS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Abstain: Council Member Franklin.

 127.2  Mayor Butts:

  Initiative by Mayor James T. Butts, Jr., recommending the introduction of an
  Ordinance amending Chapter 8 (Business, Trades, and Professions) of the
  Inglewood Municipal Code to add a new Article 9 (Housing Protection Initiative)
  for the regulation of rent increases and just cause evictions for certain covered
  residential rental units.

  4
 June 18, 2019

  It was moved By Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the following amendments be made to Ordinance No. 19-13:

  1) Residential rental units located at 435 W. Regent Street or 621 E. 99th Street
  whose property owners voluntarily provided relocation fee assistance or
  alternative residential rental housing, until April 1, 2020.
  2) Remove 1st Page 6, due to two (2) page numbers 6 included in the agenda
  packet. Prior to printing, Section D (Capital Improvement Rent Increases),
  Line 15, was amended to read “applied for more than once in a five-year
  period.”
  3) On Page 6, Section 8-122 (Evictions and Relocation Fees) has been stricken in
  its entirety and replaced with a new Section 8-122 entitled: “Just Cause for
  Eviction required for Covered Rental Units. This amendment establishes the
  Just Cause Eviction policy and removes termination of tenancy without cause,
  and adds Section 8-122.8 (Owner Move-In), and 8-122.9 (Permanent
  withdrawal of Covered rental unit from rental market) into the definition of
  Just Cause.
  4) Section 8-123 (Actions to Recover Possession Compliance with Article) has
  been changed to section 8-124, and the new section 8-123 is entitled:
  Relocation Fees. Renumbered the section to include verbiage on when tenants
  are eligible for relocation fees and the amounts (evictions pursuant to Section
  8-122.8 (Owner Move-In), and 8-122.9 (Permanent Withdrawal of Covered
  Rental Unit from Rental Market).
  5) The remaining sections formerly numbered as 8-123 (Actions to Recover
  Possession Compliance with Article), 8-124 (Civil Remedies), 8-125
  (Retaliation Prohibited), 8-126 (Enforcement Procedures), 8-127 (Landlord’s
  Rights), have been renumbered to correspond sequentially. With the new
  amendments, the sequence of section numbers has been changed.
  6) No relocation fee offered for a Just Cause eviction.
  7) This Ordinance will comply with the Ellis Act.
  8) Noticing requirements for this Ordinance to be reconciled with the State of
  California requirements.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 19-13 entitled:
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA ADDING A NEW ARTICLE 9 “HOUSING
  PROTECTION INITIATIVE” TO CHAPTER 8 OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO REGULATE RENT
  INCREASES AND JUST CAUSE EVICTIONS FOR CERTAIN
  COVERED RESIDENTIAL RENTAL UNITS AND AMENDING
  CHAPTER 2 ARTICLE 3 TO ADD A RENTAL HOUSING
  BOARD
  was introduced as amended by Mayor Butts.

  5
 June 18, 2019

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  No name given advised residents to pay attention to who they have doing
  contractor work. He congratulated the City Council for doing a great job.

  Mr. Bravo complained that the City over charged him for waste services.

  Johnathon Joseph inquired about turning in his CDBG paperwork.

  No name given inquired where she could find the motions made for Ordinance
  No. 19-13. She also inquired where she could find a hard copy of the city’s
  budget.

  Erick Holly invited the City Council and residents to the Inglewood Chambers of
  Commerce Business Networking Mixer on Thursday, June 20, 2019, at 5:30 p.m.

  Ray Davis, 2nd District, informed the public to not believe the hype.

  Morris Griffin thanked the Inglewood Police Department for their quick response
  to a 911 call he made.

  Willie Agee made a comment about being invaded.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned at the hour of 3:08 p.m.

  Approved this 16th day of July, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
